title: Clipping
subtitle: Do not draw what you cannot see: find the part of each line that lies inside the window.

why.title: Why clip
why.body: Anything outside the window is wasted effort (and could overflow the frame buffer). Clipping removes it before rasterising. The design goal: decide most cases — fully inside, fully outside — very cheaply, and compute intersections only when needed.

cohen.title: Cohen–Sutherland
cohen.body: Give each endpoint a 4-bit outcode (Top, Bottom, Right, Left): a bit is 1 if the point lies beyond that edge. If both codes are 0000 — trivially accept. If the AND of the codes is non-zero — both ends are beyond the same edge — trivially reject. Otherwise clip the outside endpoint to one window edge by intersection and repeat. For the window (10,10)–(50,50) the line (0,20)–(60,40) clips to 10,23.33 50,36.67.
cohen.steps: P1 = (0,20) is left of x = 10: outcode 0001. P2 = (60,40) is right of x = 50: outcode 0010. AND = 0000, OR ≠ 0000: undecided, so clip. Intersection with x = 10: y = 20 + (40−20)·(10−0)/(60−0).

liang.title: Liang–Barsky
liang.body: Write the line as P(t) = P₁ + t·(P₂ − P₁), 0 ≤ t ≤ 1. Each window edge gives an inequality t·p ≤ q with p = −Δx, Δx, −Δy, Δy and q = x₁ − xmin, xmax − x₁, …. Where p < 0 the line enters: raise t₀ to max(q/p); where p > 0 it leaves: lower t₁ to min(q/p). If t₀ > t₁ the line is outside. Faster than Cohen–Sutherland because it computes at most one intersection per end. Same example: 10,23.33 50,36.67.

poly.title: Polygon and text clipping
poly.body: Clipping a polygon must produce a polygon, not loose lines. Sutherland–Hodgman clips against one window edge at a time, keeping inside vertices and adding intersection points; it is right for convex polygons and can leave extra edges for concave ones, which Weiler–Atherton handles by walking the boundaries. Text is clipped per character (all-or-none), per string, or per pixel (most exact).

point.title: Point clipping
point.body: A point (x, y) is inside the window iff xmin ≤ x ≤ xmax and ymin ≤ y ≤ ymax. Everything else builds on this test.
point.steps: Window [10, 50] × [10, 50]. Is (30, 55) inside? y = 55 > 50: outside (outcode 1000, above).

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Cohen–Sutherland: outcodes, accept/reject fast, else clip an edge at a time.
  • Liang–Barsky: parametric t₀…t₁ interval, fewer intersections.
